sentences.en: Hello, and welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a podcast produced by the American Psychological
sentences.zh: 您好，欢迎收听《心理学说话》，这是一档由美国心理学会制作的播客。

sentences.en: Association.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Audrey Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。

sentences.en: In this episode, I talk with a psychologist about how marketers and even job seekers can use the six universal principles of persuasion to be successful without being manipulative.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我将与一位心理学家探讨，营销人员乃至求职者如何运用六大说服力普遍原理，在不进行操纵的情况下取得成功。

sentences.en: So you see, very small changes in the way we communicate can produce big differences because those small changes harness powerful psychological motivations inside us.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，我们沟通方式中的微小改变就能产生巨大的差异，因为这些微小的改变利用了我们内心强大的心理动机。

sentences.en: While psychologists have been able to uncover the subtle mechanics of persuasion, we also discuss how influencers can use the principles ethically,
sentences.zh: 虽然心理学家已经能够揭示说服的微妙机制，但我们也将讨论影响者如何合乎道德地运用这些原理，

sentences.en: a tactic that will lead to more effective and longer-lasting behaviors.
sentences.zh: 这一策略将带来更有效、更持久的行为。

sentences.en: Robert Cialdini has been the go-to psychology expert in marketing since his best-selling book,
sentences.zh: 自罗伯特·西奥迪尼的最畅销著作问世以来，他一直是营销领域备受推崇的心理学专家，

sentences.en: Influence, the Psychology of Persuasion, was first published in 1984.
sentences.zh: 《影响力：说服心理学》于1984年首次出版。

sentences.en: He is a Regents Professor
sentences.zh: 他是亚利桑那州立大学心理学与营销学的荣誉退休董事教授，

sentences.en: Emeritus of Psychology and Marketing at Arizona State University, as well as CEO and President
sentences.zh: 他是亚利桑那州立大学心理学与营销学的荣誉退休董事教授，

sentences.en: of the consulting company Influence at Work, which focuses on ethical influence training.
sentences.zh: 同时也是专注于道德影响力培训的咨询公司“影响力工作”的首席执行官兼总裁。

sentences.en: He recently published a new book called Persuasion, a revolutionary way to influence and persuade.
sentences.zh: 他最近出版了一本新书，名为《前说：影响与说服的革命性方法》。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Cialdini.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，西奥迪尼博士。

sentences.en: Thank you, Audrey.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，奥黛丽。

sentences.en: Good to be with you and your listeners.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能与你和你的听众交流。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, let's first talk about the theory you're most associated with, which is the six principles of persuasion.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们首先来谈谈与你联系最紧密的理论，即六大说服原理。

sentences.en: First of all, what are these six principles?
sentences.zh: 首先，这六大原理是什么？

sentences.en: Some of our listeners may not be familiar with them.
sentences.zh: 我们的一些听众可能对它们还不太熟悉。

sentences.en: And can you give them a brief description of what they are?
sentences.zh: 你能简单描述一下它们是什么吗？

sentences.en: Surely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: The first is reciprocation, the idea that in all human societies, we are trained from childhood
sentences.zh: 第一条是互惠，这个观点是，在所有人类社会中，我们从小就受到的教育是，

sentences.en: that we must give back to those who have given to us firSt. And we have very nasty names for people who don't play by those rules.
sentences.zh: 我们必须首先回报那些给予过我们帮助的人。对于不按这些规则行事的人，我们有很难听的称呼。

sentences.en: We call them moochers or takers or ingrates.
sentences.zh: 我们称他们为白吃白喝者、索取者或忘恩负义者。

sentences.en: Nobody wants to be labeled like that.
sentences.zh: 没有人愿意被贴上这样的标签。

sentences.en: So we will go to great lengths to give back to those who have given to us.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们会竭尽全力去回报那些给予过我们帮助的人。

sentences.en: There was a study done in a candy store in which half of the visitors were greeted by the manager who gave them a gift piece of chocolate upon entry.
sentences.zh: 曾有一家糖果店做过一项研究，一半的参观者在进门时受到了经理的欢迎，经理送给他们一块巧克力作为礼物。

sentences.en: They were 42% more likely to buy candy.
sentences.zh: 他们的糖果购买率高出了42%。

sentences.en: And not all of them bought chocolate.
sentences.zh: 而且并非所有人都买巧克力。

sentences.en: It wasn't that they learned that the chocolate there was good.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为他们得知那里的巧克力很好吃。

sentences.en: It's that they had been given something and they felt an obligation to give back.
sentences.zh: 而是因为他们接受了别人的东西，并感到了回报的义务。

sentences.en: A second principle is the principle of liking.
sentences.zh: 第二个原则是喜好原则。

sentences.en: No one will be surprised to know that we prefer to say yes to those we like.
sentences.zh: 我们更愿意对喜欢的人说是，这不会让人感到意外。

sentences.en: That's not a surprise.
sentences.zh: 这并不令人意外。

sentences.en: But the research suggests that there's a small thing we can do to get people to like us more.
sentences.zh: 但研究表明，我们可以做一件小事来让人们更喜欢我们。

sentences.en: For example, waiters in a restaurant, after the order is taken, if they say, to a customer, good choice, their tip goes up 13%.
sentences.zh: 例如，餐厅的服务员在点完餐后，如果对顾客说“不错的选择”，他们的小费就会增加13%。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I've heard that quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 我对此有所耳闻。

sentences.en: In a hair salon, if the stylist says, oh, that hairstyle looks great on you, her tip goes up 37%.
sentences.zh: 在美发沙龙里，如果造型师说“哦，这个发型很适合你”，她的小费就会增加37%。

sentences.en: So simply giving genuine compliments where they're warranted can be successful for all concerned.
sentences.zh: 因此，只要在适度的时候给予真诚的赞美，对所有人来说都能取得成功。

sentences.en: Another principle is the principle of what we call social proof.
sentences.zh: 另一个原则是我们所谓的社会认同原则。

sentences.en: The idea that one way we can make good decisions is to see what those around us, like us, are doing in that situation.
sentences.zh: 这个观点是，我们做出明智决策的一个方法，就是看看周围和我们相似的人在这种情况下是怎么做的。

sentences.en: There was a study done in Beijing, China.
sentences.zh: 中国北京曾做过一项研究。

sentences.en: It shows you the cross-cultural reach of this principle.
sentences.zh: 这向你展示了这一原则的跨文化影响力。

sentences.en: What they did was to go to restaurants and put on the menu a little asterisk next to certain dishes.
sentences.zh: 他们做的是去餐馆，在菜单上某些菜肴旁边加一个小星号。

sentences.en: Purchasing of those dishes immediately jumped by 13% to 20%.
sentences.zh: 这些菜肴的销量立即飙升了13%到20%。

sentences.en: Now, what did the asterisk stand for?
sentences.zh: 那么，星号代表什么呢？

sentences.en: It didn't say, this is the chef's special for tonight, or this is the specialty of the house.
sentences.zh: 它并没有说“这是今晚主厨的特荐”或“这是本店的特色菜”。

sentences.en: It said, this is one of our most popular iteMs. And it immediately became more popular because it was popular.
sentences.zh: 它说的是“这是我们最受欢迎的菜品之一”。而且因为它受欢迎，它立刻变得更受欢迎了。

sentences.en: So, social proof.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是社会认同。

sentences.en: Another principle is the principle of authority.
sentences.zh: 另一个原则是权威原则。

sentences.en: We prefer to say yes to people who can give us evidence that experts on a topic have recommended the particular steps that they are asking us to take.
sentences.zh: 我们更愿意听从那些能提供证据的人，证明某一领域的专家已经推荐了他们要求我们采取的特定步骤。

sentences.en: So, for example, in one study that my team did in hospitals with stroke patients who were sent home with exercise regimens to do while they were at home, they were 30% more
sentences.zh: 因此，例如，我的团队在医院对中风患者进行的一项研究中，这些患者出院回家时带着在家要做的锻炼方案，如果交给他们锻炼方案的人在这样做时墙上挂着他的资历和文凭，他们坚持这些锻炼方案的可能性就会提高30%

sentences.en: likely to live up to those exercise regimens if the person who gave them the exercise regimen had his credentials and diplomas on the wall when he did so.
sentences.zh: 如果交给他们锻炼方案的人在这样做时墙上挂着他的资历和文凭，他们坚持这些锻炼方案的可能性就会提高30%。

sentences.en: So, this was an expert, and people were more likely to follow the recommendations because we typically are safe in following the lead of legitimate authorities.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个专家，人们更有可能遵循这些建议，因为我们通常在遵循合法权威的引领时是安全的。

sentences.en: A fifth principle is the principle of scarcity.
sentences.zh: 第五个原则是稀缺原则。

sentences.en: People want more of those things they can have less of.
sentences.zh: 人们总是想要更多那些他们难以轻易拥有的东西。

sentences.en: So, there was one study in supermarkets that showed that of all the promotions that they did for the various brands on their stores.
sentences.zh: 因此，超市里的一项研究表明，在他们为店内各种品牌所做的一切促销活动中，

sentences.en: The one that outdistanced all the others by double was one that said only X number of items per customer.
sentences.zh: 有一项促销活动将所有其他活动远远甩在身后，达到了两倍的效果，那就是标明每位顾客只能购买X件商品的活动。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, if it's scarce, if it's rare, if it's dwindling in availability, we want it more.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果它很稀缺，如果它很罕见，如果它的供应量在减少，我们就会更想要它。

sentences.en: We want it.
sentences.zh: 我们想要它。

sentences.en: And then the final principle is commitment and consistency.
sentences.zh: 最后一个原则是承诺和一致。

sentences.en: People want to say yes to those requests that are consistent with the commitments they've already made.
sentences.zh: 人们倾向于对那些与他们已经做出的承诺相一致的请求说“好”。

sentences.en: So, for example, in a Chicago restaurant, a big problem was no-shows.
sentences.zh: 例如，在芝加哥的一家餐厅，一个很大的问题是爽约。

sentences.en: People who would call, make a reservation, and then not show for it.
sentences.zh: 人们打电话预订，然后却没有出现。

sentences.en: The owner of the restaurant tried a small technique that dramatically reduced no-shows.
sentences.zh: 餐厅老板尝试了一种小技巧，戏剧性地减少了爽约现象。

sentences.en: His receptionist used to say, thank you for calling Gordon's restaurant.
sentences.zh: 他的接待员过去常说：“感谢您致电戈登餐厅。如果您需要更改或取消预订，请打电话告知。”

sentences.en: Please call if you have to change or cancel your reservation.
sentences.zh: 如果您需要更改或取消预订，请打电话告知。

sentences.en: Instead, he asked her to say, will you please call if you have to change or cancel your reservation?
sentences.zh: 相反，他让她说：“如果您必须更改或取消预订，请您打电话告知好吗？”

sentences.en: And then to pause and let the person say, yes, of course, that produced the 67% drop in no-shows.
sentences.zh: 然后停顿一下，让对方说“好的，当然”，这使得爽约率下降了67%。

sentences.en: So, you see, very small changes in the way we communicate can produce big differences because those small changes harness powerful psychological motivations inside us.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，我们沟通方式中的微小改变就能产生巨大的差异，因为这些微小的改变利用了我们内心强大的心理动机。

sentences.en: Well, as I recently mentioned in the introduction, you recently published your latest book on something you called pre-suasion.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才在引言中提到的，你最近出版了关于你称之为“前说”的最新著作。

sentences.en: This is the idea, you say, of setting up a message before you send it to get the result you want.
sentences.zh: 你认为，这是在发送信息之前对其进行铺垫，以获得你想要的结果的想法。

sentences.en: Can you explain more about what pre-suasion is and what sort of research was conducted to demonstrate that this works?
sentences.zh: 你能更多地解释一下什么是“前说”，以及为了证明这一点进行了什么样的研究吗？

sentences.en: Surely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: So, where the book of Influence said, asked the question, what can a communicator put into a message to get people to say yes to it, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，《影响力》这本书提出了这样一个问题：沟通者可以在信息中加入什么来让人们对它说“好”，对吧？

sentences.en: These six principles, right?
sentences.zh: 这六大原则，对吧？

sentences.en: Pre-suasion asked the question, what can a communicator put into the moment before delivering the message that makes people more open and receptive to it, to make them agree
sentences.zh: 而“前说”提出的问题是：沟通者可以在传递信息之前的那个瞬间加入什么，才能让人更开放、更容易接受它，

sentences.en: agree with the message before they've encountered it?
sentences.zh: 让他们在接触信息之前就赞同它？

sentences.en: Well, that sounds like some kind of magic, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 听起来这就像某种魔法，对吧？

sentences.en: Some mind control.
sentences.zh: 某种心灵控制。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How do you get people to agree with something they don't know if they haven't heard yet?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能让人们在还没听过、甚至不知道是什么的情况下就表示同意呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Well, it's not magic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这不是魔法。

sentences.en: It's established science.
sentences.zh: 这是既定的科学。

sentences.en: And the key is, if the communicator gets an individual to focus on a particular concept or idea that is the central
sentences.zh: 关键在于，如果沟通者让个人专注于某个特定的概念或想法，而这正是尚未发生的信息的核心方面，

sentences.en: aspect of the message that's yet to occur, people will now focus on that central aspect when they encounter it.
sentences.zh: 人们在遇到这个核心方面时就会关注它。

sentences.en: They will have been sensitized to that kind of information.
sentences.zh: 他们对这种信息已经有了敏感度。

sentences.en: I'll give you an example, a research example.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个例子，一个研究的例子。

sentences.en: A study was done with an online furniture store.
sentences.zh: 有一项针对在线家具店的研究。

sentences.en: They specialized in sofas.
sentences.zh: 他们专门销售沙发。

sentences.en: Half of the visitors to their website encountered a landing page with fluffy clouds as the background wallpaper of that site.
sentences.zh: 他们网站的一半访客看到的是一个以蓬松的云朵作为网站背景壁纸的落地页。

sentences.en: Those individuals then rated comfort of sofas as more important to them.
sentences.zh: 这些访客随后将沙发的舒适度评为对他们更重要的因素。

sentences.en: They searched the site for comfort-related features of the sofas, and they preferred to purchase more
sentences.zh: 他们在网站上搜索沙发与舒适度相关的特征，并且更倾向于购买更舒适的家具，

sentences.en: comfortable furniture because the first thing they were focused on was softness in those clouds.
sentences.zh: 因为他们首先关注的是那些云朵的柔软度。

sentences.en: Now, the other half of the visitors were sent to a site with small coins, pennies, in the background wallpaper.
sentences.zh: 现在，另外一半的访客被引导到一个背景壁纸上有小硬币、即一美分的网站。

sentences.en: They then rated price as a more important feature for them in buying a sofa.
sentences.zh: 然后他们将价格评为购买沙发时更重要的功能。

sentences.en: They searched the site for cost-related information, and they preferred to purchase more inexpensive furniture.
sentences.zh: 他们在网站上搜索与成本相关的信息，并且更倾向于购买更便宜的家具。

sentences.en: So wherever they were sent first, now they prioritize that idea, that concept in what they encountered next.
sentences.zh: 因此，无论他们首先被引导到哪里，他们现在都会在接下来的接触中优先考虑那个想法、那个概念。

sentences.en: The interesting thing was that when they were asked afterwards, by the way, did that background on the landing page make any difference to you and how you chose?
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当事后问他们：“顺便问一下，落地页上的那个背景对你和你的选择有什么影响吗？”

sentences.en: They laughed.
sentences.zh: 他们笑了。

sentences.en: They said, of course not.
sentences.zh: 他们说：“当然没有。”

sentences.en: I'm a freestanding entity.
sentences.zh: “我是一个独立的个体。”

sentences.en: I make my decisions based on my internal preferences.
sentences.zh: “我根据自己的内在偏好做出决定。”

sentences.en: They never recognized that their internal preferences had been shaped by what they saw firSt. Well, let's take this idea of persuasion.
sentences.zh: 他们从没有意识到自己的内在偏好其实已经被他们首先看到的东西塑造了。好了，让我们来看看这个说服的概念。假设我要去参加求职面试，或者也许我要向老板要求晋升或加薪。我该如何进行铺垫以获得我想要的东西呢？

sentences.en: Let's say I'm going for a job interview, or maybe I'm asking my boss for a promotion or a raise.
sentences.zh: 假设我要去参加求职面试，或者也许我要向老板要求晋升或加薪。

sentences.en: How do I set it up to get what I want?
sentences.zh: 我该如何进行铺垫以获得我想要的东西呢？

sentences.en: Let's take the job interview.
sentences.zh: 我们以求职面试为例。

sentences.en: That's a classic one.
sentences.zh: 这是一个经典的例子。

sentences.en: We typically go into a situation.
sentences.zh: 我们通常会进入这样一个情境。

sentences.en: There's an evaluator sitting across the table, sometimes more than one.
sentences.zh: 桌子对面坐着一个评估员，有时不止一个。

sentences.en: And what we are typically trained to say is, thank you for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 我们通常受到的训练是说：“谢谢您邀请我来。我一定会回答您的所有问题。”

sentences.en: I want to be sure to answer all of the questions you have of me.
sentences.zh: 我一定会回答您的所有问题。

sentences.en: Here's what I would recommend based on persuasion.
sentences.zh: 以下是我根据说服原理建议的做法。

sentences.en: We should say one more thing before the interview begins.
sentences.zh: 在面试开始前，我们应该多说一句话。

sentences.en: But you know, I'm curious.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，我很好奇。

sentences.en: I have a question for you.
sentences.zh: 我有个问题想问你。

sentences.en: Why did you invite me here today?
sentences.zh: 你今天为什么邀请我来这里？

sentences.en: What was it about my candidacy that attracted you to me?
sentences.zh: 我的什么条件吸引了你？

sentences.en: Now what you will find as these individuals will go into your resume, focusing themselves on your strengths, all of the most positive things about your resume, your qualifications?
sentences.zh: 现在你会发现，这些人会去查阅你的简历，将注意力集中在你的优势上，集中在你简历中最积极的方面、你的资格上？

sentences.en: And the interview will begin with that as the, as the, uh, fundament.
sentences.zh: 面试将以这一点作为基础开始。

sentences.en: That's the frame of the interview, your strengths.
sentences.zh: 这就是面试的框架，即你的优势。

sentences.en: Now, I have an acquaintance who claims he's gotten three straight better jobs in a row using this strategy, this persuasive strategy.
sentences.zh: 现在，我有一个熟人声称他通过使用这种策略、这种说服策略，连续得到了三份更好的工作。

sentences.en: It makes sense when you think about it.
sentences.zh: 仔细想想，这确实很有道理。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: How can it hurt?
sentences.zh: 这有什么坏处呢？

sentences.en: How can it hurt?
sentences.zh: 这有什么坏处呢？

sentences.en: You're focusing people on your strengths.
sentences.zh: 你在引导人们关注你的优势。

sentences.en: And also when you hear them describe your strengths, you know what their values are, what the things they're looking for, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，当你听到他们描述你的优势时，你就知道了他们的价值观是什么，他们在寻找什么，对吧？

sentences.en: Those are the reasons they brought you in.
sentences.zh: 这些就是他们把你招进来的原因。

sentences.en: You can now embellish on those features of your, uh, your background and credentials.
sentences.zh: 你现在可以进一步阐述你的背景和资历中的这些特点。

sentences.en: Another thing I want to address is the idea of ethics and persuasion.
sentences.zh: 我要讨论的另一件事是道德与说服的概念。

sentences.en: You know, as a psychologist who instructs companies on how to persuade others, people, how, consumers, how do you convince them to do so without stepping over that ethical line
sentences.zh: 你知道，作为一个指导公司如何说服他人的心理学家，你怎么能说服人们，让他们在不跨越道德底线进入操纵的情况下做到这一点呢？

sentences.en: into manipulation, let's say?
sentences.zh: 比如说？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, we've, my team has recently completed a piece of research on what happens to organizations that don't apply ethical rules to the way that they treat their
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们的团队最近完成了一项关于以下情况的研究：那些不对对待客户、客户、潜在客户的规则应用道德规范，并且在展示这些信息时具有欺骗性和不诚实的组织，会发生什么情况。

sentences.en: customers, their clients, their prospects, and who are deceptive, dishonest in the presentation of that information.
sentences.zh: 他们的客户、潜在客户，以及在提供信息时具有欺骗性和不诚实的组织，会发生什么情况。

sentences.en: What happens is some people inside the organization, inside the company, feel uncomfortable with this kind of duplicity, this requirement that they be dishonest as part of
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，组织内部、公司内部的一些人对这种两面三刀感到不舒服，这种将不诚实作为工作一部分的要求让他们感到不适。

sentences.en: their job.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作。

sentences.en: It creates, um, emotional distress in them.
sentences.zh: 这给他们带来了情绪上的困扰。

sentences.en: They're agitated.
sentences.zh: 他们感到焦虑。

sentences.en: They're upset by having to do this.
sentences.zh: 他们对必须这样做感到心烦意乱。

sentences.en: And our research shows, as a consequence, they perform their jobs less well because they're upset.
sentences.zh: 我们的研究表明，因此，由于他们感到心烦意乱，他们的工作表现也会变差。

sentences.en: They're more likely to leave the organization, right?
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能离开这个组织，对吧？

sentences.en: Which creates big turnover costs for any company that, uh, that, that chooses an unethical approach, right?
sentences.zh: 对于任何选择采用不道德手段的公司来说，这会产生巨大的员工流失成本，对吧？

sentences.en: But thirdly, when those people who are uncomfortable with cheating leave, and what's left is a precipitate of employees who are comfortable with
sentences.zh: 但第三，当那些对作弊感到不舒服的人离开后，留下的是一类对

sentences.en: cheating, we find they will cheat the company.
sentences.zh: 作弊习以为常的员工，我们发现他们会欺骗公司。

sentences.en: The company has selected for dishonest people.
sentences.zh: 这家公司筛选出了不诚实的人。

sentences.en: Those people who lie for you will lie to you.
sentences.zh: 那些为你撒谎的人也会对你撒谎。

sentences.en: These will be the people who pad their expense accounts, who run under the table deals with vendors and suppliers, who steal equipment, and so on.
sentences.zh: 这些人会虚报差旅费、与供应商私下进行暗箱交易、窃取设备等等。

sentences.en: So it's against their own best interest and bottom line.
sentences.zh: 所以这违背了他们自身的最佳利益和底线。

sentences.en: That's exactly right, Audrey.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，奥黛丽。

sentences.en: It's, it's, this is the reason why when I speak to leaders of various organizations, I tell them that they should be scrupulously honest, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当我与各个组织的领导者交谈时，我告诉他们应该绝对诚实，对吧？

sentences.en: Anything less is going, anything less is going to drive away their most honest employees and give them the, the headache
sentences.zh: 任何低于这个标准的事物都会赶走他们最诚实的员工，并给他们带来

sentences.en: of having to manage dishonest employees inside their organizational envelope.
sentences.zh: 不得不在组织内部管理不诚实员工的头痛问题。

sentences.en: So circling back to the original six principles that we talked about at the beginning, how can people recognize when someone is using them unethically or being manipulative?
sentences.zh: 那么，回到我们一开始讨论的最初六个原则，人们如何识别别人何时在不道德地使用这些策略或具有操纵性？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Sometimes you can't tell until the transaction is over and you realize that you've been, you've been fooled or duped or not fully informed.
sentences.zh: 有时你直到交易结束才会发现，那时你才意识到自己被愚弄了、被欺骗了或者信息不完全。

sentences.en: You know, we, we, in my company, we sometimes have technological issues that need to be solved and we need to contract somebody who comes in to solve them and
sentences.zh: 你知道，在我的公司里，我们有时会遇到需要解决的技术问题，我们需要承包某人进来解决这些问题，而

sentences.en: people will claim expertise.
sentences.zh: 人们会声称自己有专业知识。

sentences.en: Oh yes, we can do this.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，我们能做到这一点。

sentences.en: We have a long history of being able to solve this particular problem.
sentences.zh: 我们在解决这个特定问题方面有着悠久的历史。

sentences.en: And then we find out that was just to get us to sign the contract.
sentences.zh: 然后我们发现，那只是为了让我们签署合同。

sentences.en: They claim to have authority when they didn't.
sentences.zh: 他们声称自己拥有并没有的权限。

sentences.en: And as a consequence, our only redress is to say, we will never do business with you again.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们唯一的补救措施就是说，我们再也不会和你们做生意了。

sentences.en: We will never testify.
sentences.zh: 我们永远不会作证。

sentences.en: We will never give a testimonial in your behalf.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会代你发表感谢信或好评。

sentences.en: In fact, we'll tell all our friends not to do business with you.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们会告诉我们所有的朋友不要和你们做生意。

sentences.en: That's the long-term consequence of the unethical use of these strategies.
sentences.zh: 这就是不道德使用这些策略的长期后果。

sentences.en: Now, that's not to say that people who use these strategies always use them dishonestly.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不是说使用这些策略的人总是出于不诚实的目的。

sentences.en: The last time I bought a television set, I was in an appliance store.
sentences.zh: 我上次买电视机时，正在一家电器店里。

sentences.en: I wasn't really looking for a new TV, but I saw a great deal on a big screen TV that I knew had been rated very well by consumer reports.
sentences.zh: 我并不是真的在找一台新电视，但我看到了一台大屏幕电视的大促销，我知道它在消费者报告中获得了极高的评价。

sentences.en: And a salesman came up to me, said, I see you're interested in this set here.
sentences.zh: 一个售货员向我走来，说，我看到你对这台电视感兴趣。

sentences.en: I can understand why.
sentences.zh: 我能理解为什么。

sentences.en: That's a great price for that model.
sentences.zh: 这个型号的价格太棒了。

sentences.en: But I should tell you, that's our last one.
sentences.zh: 但我得告诉你，这是我们最后一台了。

sentences.en: And I just got a call from a woman to say that she might be in today.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚接到一个女人的电话，说她可能今天会来。

sentences.en: To get it.
sentences.zh: 把它买走。

sentences.en: To get it.
sentences.zh: 把它买走。

sentences.en: Audrey, 20 minutes later, I'm wheeling out of the store with that set in my cart.
sentences.zh: 奥黛丽，20分钟后，我推着购物车把那台电视运出了商店。

sentences.en: And I'm the guy who wrote the book on this.
sentences.zh: 而我就是写过这方面书的人。

sentences.en: I'm still susceptible to it, right?
sentences.zh: 我仍然会受到它的影响，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, here's what I did the following day.
sentences.zh: 现在，我第二天做了这样一件事。

sentences.en: I went back to that store to see if that set was still an empty space on the shelf.
sentences.zh: 我回到那家店，看看那台电视的位置是不是在货架上空出来了。

sentences.en: Was it really the last one?
sentences.zh: 它真的是最后一台吗？

sentences.en: Or had they just gone to the storeroom and replaced it with another?
sentences.zh: 还是他们只是去了储藏室又拿了一台来替换？

sentences.en: And that scarcity principle was being exploited to get me to comply.
sentences.zh: 当时那个稀缺原则正被用来促使我妥协。

sentences.en: It wasn't a genuine piece of information that I could use to improve my outcomes in the situation.
sentences.zh: 这不是一条我能用来改善这种情况下结果的真实信息。

sentences.en: It turns out there was an empty space.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，确实空了一个位置。

sentences.en: It was true.
sentences.zh: 那是真的。

sentences.en: So here's what I did.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了这样的事。

sentences.en: I went back to my office.
sentences.zh: 我回到了办公室。

sentences.en: I went online and I provided a customer review that praised that store and that salesperson because in that situation, he was not my enemy.
sentences.zh: 我上网写了一篇客户评论，赞扬了那家店和那个售货员，因为在这种情况下，他不是我的敌人。

sentences.en: He was my ally in the process of getting something good by giving me honest information about true scarcity.
sentences.zh: 他是我的盟友，通过向我提供关于真正稀缺性的诚实信息，帮助我获得了好东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: Under those circumstances, I was happy to partner with him.
sentences.zh: 在那种情况下，我很高兴与他合作。
